findings: BTZ_1.tex l.842-846: the printed proof needs no smoothness of tau_Sigma beyond Lipschitz along the curve. The bound ell <= int sqrt(5 - 2 tau') and the step 'tau' <= 5/2' only use that the developed velocity is non-timelike a.e. (spacelike) and that tau is absolutely continuous along a straight piece. Both hold for any graph whose development is spacelike Lipschitz: such a graph is automatically locally Lipschitz in (r, theta), because D(tau, r, theta) = D(0, r, theta) + tau * d_tau D with d_tau D null, and a uniformly spacelike chord kappa |Delta F|^2 <= minkQ(Delta F) bounds |Delta tau| by the smooth Delta r, Delta(r theta), Delta(r theta^2) (locallyLipschitzOn_of_spacelikeDevelopment). So part (ii) holds for Lipschitz (in particular piecewise smooth, continuous) graphs, which is the form l.1602 uses on Sigma_0.

BTZ_1.tex l.835-838: with the stated slope |theta'_gamma| <= 2pi/r_n on ]r_{n+1}, r_n[ and r <= r_n, r^2 theta'^2 <= 4 pi^2, so the printed constant 5 should be 1 + 4pi^2 (the strict row's finding, already recorded at edist_le_seg; here the same constant (1 + 2 pi^2) per unit dr is used). Harmless: any constant works.

BTZ_1.tex l.846 ('By completeness of Sigma, the length ell of gamma is infinite'): the formal argument goes through the contrapositive as the strict proof does (a finite-length broken line gives a Cauchy sequence whose limit would be at positive radius). In the Lipschitz setting the last step uses that the pulled-length topology is finer than the strip's (Causal.Flat.SpacelikeDevelopment.continuous_toSpace) instead of the strict clamp estimate, which needed delta >= delta_0 > 0 on an annulus (a C^1 fact).
questions: Reading of 'spacelike' for a non-smooth graph (l.786): taken as Causal.Flat.SpacelikeDevelopment of graphDev g R (locally embedded, locally a c-Lipschitz graph with c < 1 in some Minkowski frame), the notion in which T-btz-cauchy-spear's Sigma_0 is complete (OQ-152 (b)). The paper only defines spacelike for piecewise smooth graphs (Lemma 2.7, delta > 0 on each smooth domain). That the paper's piecewise smooth spacelike graphs satisfy this reading is not proved (it is the bridge in kb_proposals); the row's partial status already rests on T-btz-scope.

kb_proposals: A graph whose development D(g(r,theta), r, theta) is a Causal.Flat.SpacelikeDevelopment is locally Lipschitz on the strip (GX.E0Surgery.locallyLipschitzOn_of_spacelikeDevelopment): D is affine in tau along the null d_tau D, and SpacelikeDevelopment.exists_uniform_nhds (kappa |Delta F|^2 <= minkQ Delta F on a neighbourhood) bounds |Delta tau|.

For a curve Gamma with eventually non-timelike chords, the velocity is non-timelike (GX.E0Surgery.minkQ_nonneg_of_hasDerivAt, via hasDerivAt_iff_tendsto_slope and continuous_minkQ); this is the a.e. 'integrand well defined' of length estimates on Lipschitz spacelike surfaces.

In a completeness-by-contradiction argument on Causal.Flat.PulledLength F, Causal.Flat.SpacelikeDevelopment.continuous_toSpace replaces any metric lower bound near the limit: the limit in the pulled length is a limit in X.
